Data: [TidyTuesday 2026-10-27](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-10-27).

The data lists every sofa and armchair on ikea.com in 50 countries, with prices converted to US dollars.
To compare countries, I kept the 111 products that are on sale in at least 30 countries.
For each product, I divided its price in a country by its median price over all the countries that sell it.
A country's dot is the median of those ratios.

Prices differ a lot.
A typical product costs 1.65 times its median price in Mexico and 0.76 times in Thailand, which makes Mexico more than twice as dear.
Morocco, Israel, Colombia and Jordan follow Mexico, while Japan, the Philippines and South Korea sit with Thailand at the cheap end.
Most of western Europe lands close to 1.
The Netherlands and Austria sit at 1.00, and Italy, Sweden and Belgium are within a point of it.

Some cautions.
The prices were converted at one day's exchange rates, so a swing in a currency moves its country.
The prices are not adjusted for local taxes or for the cost of living, and IKEA does not stock every product everywhere.
The number of products compared goes from 32 to 107 across countries, so the countries at the low end of that range rest on fewer products.
